newsitem.title: UK: ALUMINIUM STEADY, BUT OTHER LME METALS WILT AT END.
newsitem.headline: ALUMINIUM STEADY, BUT OTHER LME METALS WILT AT END.

text.p: Most base metal prices sagged during the latter part of a dull Monday LME session, pulled down by copper, although aluminium was an exception, traders said.
Aluminium was partially immune to the lethargy elsewhere, as this market is perceived to be nearing the end of a downside technical correction. However, there was little significant interest overall.
"There was a bit of action on the kerb, but that was it really," one trader said.

The aluminium market shrugged off a rise in June IPAI producer inventories, and rallied away from near $1,730 support on fund buying. By the close prices were at $1,750, up $4, with last week's $1,775 highs back in sight, some said.
Copper fell prey to stale bull liquidation this afternoon, with some sell-stops triggered, and the market briefly tested $2,270 before ending at $2,274, down $14.
Traders see depressed physical conditions and reports from the U.S. that North American copper producers are expected to move to the sell side of the market leaving prices vulnerable.
Zinc wobbled as well during the kerb, but still finished just $2 lower at $1,545. September tightness continues to cushion the market, with cash/threes at $155/175 backwardation.
Nickel extended earlier declines during the afternoon, with the retreat accelerating on the kerb as the market fell through $6,900.

In Canada, meanwhile, the Falconbridge Sudbury strike is continuing into a second week. On Monday, the union said it was waiting for a response to its proposal on shift schedules. Last trade was at $6,860, down $225.

Lead lurched lower this afternoon as well, briefly threatening to fall under $600 and set a new 22-month low before modest support near "the figure" emerged. Nevertheless, last trade was at $605, down $9.
Tin matched the trend, and closed $85 lower at $5,520, while alloy ended at a steady $1,540/45 a tonne.
